question: Does chance-weighted root selection use the improved weighted-frontier support more effectively than adversarial board selection?
motivation: Three preselected fatal-choice traces retain the safe comparator in the matrix. Full-population risk can be overridden by the sampled board payoffs and additional row charges.
prior_findings: Root expectation without this frontier was inconclusive (165/160/166 terminal fatalities). Frontier alone improved support but not decisions (158/164). This tests their interaction, not a new validation set.

arms.2: Same posterior-distributed columns plus maximum mean

primary_comparison: mode2 minus mode1 terminal fatality and paired saved/new counts
secondary: mode1 minus mode0 column-sampling effect; mode2 minus mode0 overall change
model: same frozen repairs-v4 graphs from frontier action comparison
correctness: Original root mode0 must match all1338 frontier decisions.
Modes1/2 must use identical columns, nodes and payoff cells on the three diagnostic histories.
Run original engine and posterior selector tests.
limits: Reused development positions, not independent strength evidence.
Prior selection of this interaction follows negative results; no multiple-testing-adjusted claim.
No automatic release or constant tuning.
